chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Munqari, from the one he mentioned, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who divorces his wife while they have a child, which of them is more entitled to the child? He said: The wife is more entitled to the child as long as she has not married.

The meaning in this report is one of two things: one of them is that she is more entitled if she accepts the same wage that others take for the nursing and upbringing of the child, which indicates that.
ai.seo_question: Who has priority for child custody after divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) clarifying the mother’s right to custody (*hadanah*) post-divorce, contingent upon her acceptance of a wage (*ujrah*) comparable to that of a wet nurse. This ruling highlights the distinction between the right of physical care and the father’s financial obligation, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence for determining child custody arrangements.
